head: claude/mi279-ci-skip-directive-detector
title: U3: the scheduled PR watcher can now say “CI was never allowed to run on this head” — and this PR omits `draft` to settle BL-20260903's second clause
body:
**Tier-1** — one new pure module, one scheduled watcher extended, one workflow self-test step. No `src/`, no `config/`, no VM, no order path. Lane: OPS, MI-279, unit **U3**.

⚠️ **This PR is also the second half of `BL-20260903`'s experiment.** It is opened through `pr-opener.yml` from a request file that **OMITS `draft` entirely**, because that row's criterion requires the default be verified UNCHANGED in the same pass:

> *The default must be verified UNCHANGED in the same pass: a request file that OMITS `draft` entirely must still produce `draft: true`, since `true` is the correct default and a fix that inverts it would arm auto-merge on every Tier-2/3 PR the relay opens.*

The first half was settled by #11966 (request carried `"draft": false`, PR came back `draft: false`). Whichever way this one comes back is reported afterwards — **the outcome is asserted nowhere in the diff.** If it comes back `false`, the fix inverted the default, that is a Tier-2/3 safety regression, and it is the far more important finding.

## The defect

A push whose head commit message carries a CI-skip directive runs **no workflow at all**, and the directive is honoured **anywhere in the message, body included**. The PR then reads `blocked` with zero check runs — which renders identically to *CI is queued*, to *a merge conflict suppressed the runs*, and to *required checks never attached*.

`CLAUDE.md` documents exactly one cause for `total_count: 0` (a merge conflict) and sends the reader to `mergeable_state`. On this failure that reads **`blocked`, not `dirty`**, so the documented check leads to the wrong conclusion.

## The remedy I first reached for is impossible, and that is the design note

A **CI guard cannot catch this**, because the defect is that no workflow runs — the check would never execute on the commit it targets. The same disqualifies `armed-branch-push-watch.yml` and every other `on: push` detector: the push is exactly what was skipped. A **scheduled** reader is the only surface that can see it, which is why this lives beside `pr_queue_latency.py` and not in `scripts/ci/`.

## Live controls, not only planted ones

Against the real commits of PR #11937:

| head | message | grade | checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cd43ff61` | clean subject, directive quoted on body line 9 | `body`, line 9, token named | `total_count: 0` |
| `719efb9d` (its own ancestor, same branch) | no directive | `absent` | ran |

Same branch, same base, same workflow set, same permissions — the only difference is the token. **And the remedy is evidenced too:** pushing a directive-free commit took #11937 from `total_count: 0` to checks running.

## A third dimension, folded into neither count

`pr_queue_latency` already keeps quiescence (*has anyone moved this?*) and mergeability (*could anyone merge it?*) apart. This adds *was CI ever allowed to run on this head at all?* — folded into neither, because its owner and remedy are different again: the PR is owed **a new commit, by its author**.

`explains_no_checks` is narrow on purpose: silent when a conflict already explains the emptiness, mirroring `ci_settle`'s own rule that `dirty` is reported ahead of `no_checks`. Re-attributing that would swap one confident wrong answer for another.

Four states, never collapsed: `absent` / `subject` / `body` / `unreadable`. `None` is *we did not look*; an empty string is a real read and grades `absent`. Prose naming the directive **without brackets is deliberately not a match**, so the module and its backlog row can describe the defect without causing it.

## A self-test bug found while adding to it

`pr_queue_latency._self_test` printed its PASS/FAIL summary **before** the new assertions ran, so a failure in them would have been reported as `0 failures`. The summary now prints last, and a planted break was confirmed to reach it (rc=1, failing assertion named).

## Verification

`ci_skip_directive --self-test` 15/15 · `pr_queue_latency --self-test` 0 failures · full `run_guards.py` · `check_pr_landing` · `check_backlog_refs --base origin/main` · `check_claim_basis` 0 findings.
